text:
---
description: Dispatch implementation for one or more planned tasks by workstream
argument-hint: "[task number(s) from docs/tasks/[TICKET]-todo.md, a description naming planned task(s), or <TICKET> review fixes]"
---
Dispatch `executor` agents for implementation.

`/build` owns orchestration and integration. The executor owns implementation
discipline, tests, verification, and scoped local commits.
Resolve the target per `../references/target-selection.md`, and announce it ("Using: <target>") before anything else.

Read the selected plan's header, task index, dependencies/checkpoints, and
Verification Strategy. Resolve full task packets from its designated local
todo or external tracker, honoring project artifact locations; default to
`docs/tasks/[TICKET]-todo.md` only when no alternative is designated. If the
authoritative packets cannot be read, report the missing source and stop;
do not reconstruct them from summaries or a stale local copy.
Check the plan's own header before dispatching anything:

- The **plan's** `Status` must read `Approved`. `Draft`, `Needs replan` or
  `Superseded` stops dispatch and returns to `/plan`.

- The **spec's** `Status` must still read `Approved` too. A plan approved
  against a spec that has since gone `Needs reapproval` or `Superseded` is
  building to requirements nobody currently stands behind — check the spec
  header, not just the plan's record of it.

- Retrieve the pinned spec and diff it:
  `git show <sha>:<spec path>` against the working copy.

A difference is not automatically a stale plan; an editorial fix changes the
file without changing behavior. Read the diff before deciding. Editorial only →
re-pin the new commit, note it, proceed. Behavioral, **or any change to the
`Status` line** → the plan is stale: set it `Needs replan` and stop. If the
pinned sha no longer resolves (rebased or squashed away), treat the plan as
`Needs replan` rather than guessing. Report which path was taken; a difference
waved through without the diff defeats the check
(`../references/spec-pin.md`).

Read each selected task's `Status:` in the todo as committed at `HEAD` (`git
show HEAD:<todo path>`), not the working copy. `Done` means the commit that
completed the task is already in this branch: skip it and report it as already
complete. `Pending` tasks are dispatched as usual. A re-run after a crash, a
compaction, or in a fresh session therefore resumes at the first unfinished
task instead of redoing or guessing. A `Done` task whose acceptance criteria
the integrated verification later fails is not trusted for being marked: it
returns to an executor like any other failure. External trackers keep their own
status; update it at the same point instead.

A task the plan gives to a later stage or to a person — a browser check that
`/test` runs, a measurement on production-size data, a sign-off — is not
`/build`'s to implement, whatever workstream it sits in. Do not dispatch an
executor for it, leave its `Status` as the plan set it, and do not count it as
unimplemented: when every task `/build` owns is implemented and the
checkpoints pass, report **BUILD COMPLETE** and list those tasks under
**Handed on**, each with its stage (`/test`) or person. A checkpoint that
depends on such a task runs without it and says so.
For each selected task resolve:
- outcome and acceptance criteria;
- dependencies;
- planned workstream;
- expected file/area scope;
- verification;
- required skills.

Honor `/plan`'s workstream assignment. For a task in an older approved plan that
records no workstream, infer one using the same rules. Work with no approved
plan is not `/build`'s input: it goes to `/plan` first. Stop before dispatch when the recorded workstream
conflicts with dependencies, or when the task is ambiguous — meaning you cannot
state the expected observable behavior from the packet and plan without
inventing a decision. Report what is missing instead of guessing.
Use **one executor per workstream, not one per task**.
- first selected task in a workstream -> fresh named `executor`;
- tasks inside a workstream stay sequential and follow dependency order;

- among dependency-ready tasks, dispatch those with no checkpoint dependency
  before checkpoint-gated ones.

A task whose spec or task packet links a Figma design gets `figma-executor`
in place of `executor`, fresh or resumed. Every other task gets `executor`.
The two share one body and one set of gates. Only the Figma copy loads the
Figma tools, and only the read-only design-to-code set, because a subagent
loads every granted tool in full on every call (ADR 0118).

A resume after the cache expired rewrites the whole context at full price. A
large context also slows and degrades the executor.

Run sequential executors in the existing ticket checkout; omit an isolation
argument. The executor definition deliberately has no unconditional isolation.
For concurrent writers, explicitly set `isolation: worktree` on each dispatch
and verify its returned checkout path before accepting implementation evidence.
If the runtime cannot provide separate checkouts, queue the workstreams.
The test-engineer keeps its own isolated checkout, and reviewers keep
independent contexts (docs/adr/0058).

Before dispatch, establish the assigned Git checkout and branch. Refuse the main
checkout's default branch, detached HEAD, or unverifiable Git state. When the
project provides executable `bin/worktree-doctor.sh`, run it with
`--infrastructure` and require exit 0. The contract is a fast, nonmutating check
that needs no installed project dependencies; nonzero output names the repair.
If the main registered checkout provides the doctor but the ticket checkout
lacks it, reconcile the project runner changes first. Do not force arbitrary
merges or refresh dependencies merely because a ticket is behind the default
branch. Claude's dispatch hook enforces this; other runtimes must perform the
same readiness check explicitly.

When the project's worktree setup script (such as `bin/worktree-setup.sh`)
fails, do not replay its steps by hand:
- report the failing step and its error output;

- use an override only when the project documents one, and name it in the
  report;

- with no documented override, the checkout is not ready: report BUILD
  BLOCKED with route `owner`;
- never copy an improvised workaround into executor packets.

When the tree has failures before the change, record them once before
dispatch. Run the suite once with machine-readable output: JUnit XML (for
example `--log-junit <file>` or `--reporter=junit`) or the runner's
equivalent. Save it in the scratchpad. Do not rerun the suite to re-parse its
text output. Each later comparison writes JUnit too and compares by test
identity:

```bash
python3 ~/.claude/skills/executor-development-discipline/scripts/junit-diff.py <baseline.xml> <after.xml>
```

It exits 1 on a new failure, a newly skipped test, or a baseline test missing
from the later run. Pass the baseline path to executors in the packet.

Honor every checkpoint recorded in the plan. A task ordered after a checkpoint
is not dependency-ready until that checkpoint's criteria have been executed and
passed — run them at the boundary; do not take an upstream executor's task
completion as the checkpoint result. This applies with force to
contract-separated workstreams: never dispatch the downstream workstream before
its named contract checkpoint passes, even when executors are idle and the work
"could start."
Send only what is needed to start correctly:
- task/outcome;
- acceptance criteria;
- dependencies;
- workstream;

- assigned checkout path and execution mode (sequential inherited checkout or
  concurrent isolated checkout);
- expected scope;
- verification;
- `required_skills`;
- `is_last_selected_task_in_workstream: yes|no`;

- the todo path and task id whose `Status:` the executor sets to `Done` in its
  completing commit;

- for a fresh executor on a later task: the previous handoff report and the
  workstream's commit ids so far;
- the test-baseline JUnit path, when one was recorded;
- pre-authorization `TD-###` ids and external-tool blockers the plan records;
- workstream verification command when applicable;

- useful pointers to project/module rules, one or two precedents, and any shared
  contract/invariant;
- the path of the project's `REVIEW.md` from the base branch, when there is one.

Prefer pointers over pasted documents. Do not dump the full spec, plan, project
rules, investigation transcript, or another agent's output. The previous
handoff report is the one exception.
Every fresh executor receives:

```text
required_skills:
  - executor-development-discipline
  - test-driven-development
```

That baseline is preloaded by the executor definition. Do not paste or invoke it
again.

Add a task-specific skill only when its methodology is materially required.
Typical examples:
- shared/public API or contract -> `api-and-interface-design`;
- compatibility/deprecation/migration -> `deprecation-and-migration`;

- auth, permissions, secrets, or sensitive trust boundary ->
  `security-and-hardening`.

- a task whose spec or task packet links a Figma design ->
  `figma-design-to-code` (needs the Figma MCP server and the skill fetched by
  `tools/setup/fetch-figma-skill.sh`; when either is missing, the
  executor reports the blocker instead of building from memory of the design);

- adding or reshaping a React component's API (props, compound components,
  providers) -> `vercel-composition-patterns`;
- Vite config or plugins -> `vite`; Vitest tests, mocking or config -> `vitest`.

Never select `browser-testing-with-devtools` for an executor. Executors hold no
browser tools; test-engineer does (docs/adr/0070).
The executor invokes only additional skills selected by `/build`.

**Sequential by default** (ADR 0136). Run workstreams one after another, in
dependency order, so each executor builds on the code already merged. Run them
in parallel only when the user asks for it in this run. Then read
`../references/parallel-workstreams.md` before any dispatch and
follow it: it decides which workstreams may run at once and what the
completion report must state.

Use the executor's configured default model for routine work. Override upward
only for high-risk work where a wrong decision is expensive to undo — e.g.
irreversible migrations, concurrency/consistency invariants, security-sensitive
boundaries, or novel external contracts.

Never blind-retry. A retry needs new evidence, a code/config/environment change,
or a materially different hypothesis.

Do not broaden tools, permissions, scope, or external write authority for
convenience. Surface a genuine capability boundary.

When an executor reports a blocker or a task-packet conflict (acceptance
criteria infeasible against the repository, contradicted by the code, or
requiring an absent decision):

- stop that workstream at the blocked task; do not re-dispatch the same task
  hoping for a different reading;

- continue other workstreams only if they do not depend on the blocked task or
  a checkpoint behind it;
- record the blocker in the completion report.

For sequential and parallel builds alike, run affected checks after each
integration and the plan's **Verification Strategy → Integrated** commands
on the final integrated tree. Reuse an identical successful check only when
no intervening change could affect its result. For a selected subset, report
that scope without claiming unselected behavior complete; do not silently
drop or rewrite required commands that cannot run.

When the candidate changes a deployed runtime entrypoint or critical end-to-end
path, run the repository-defined smoke check in the appropriate safe
environment.

BUILD does not prove browser-dependent acceptance criteria: actual rendering,
browser APIs, navigation, console, or network behavior. Executors have no
browser tools. List each such criterion in the completion message as
`Needs real-browser check: <REQ id> — <criterion>`. Do not count component
tests as evidence for it. `/test` runs next, and test-engineer runs the check.

Rerun every selected task's `Change-surface search` on the integrated tree. A
hit no task changed and no task lists as unchanged goes back to the owning
executor: an integration can drop a location one workstream handled and
another reverted.

Check executor evidence against the selected acceptance criteria and shared
invariants under the development skill's completion rules. A green command
or executor summary alone does not establish an outcome its checks did not
exercise. Return an evidence gap to the owning workstream's executor for
focused verification, resumed or fresh under §2's rule; route missing plan decisions or behavior conflicts under §2.

Confirm affected project documentation matches the integrated result under
`../references/documentation-practices.md` §Project documentation. Return stale
in-scope sections to the owning executor; report missing scope through the
existing blocker process rather than declaring the documentation complete.
`/build` ends in exactly one of two reports.
**BUILD COMPLETE** — only when all of the following hold:

- all selected tasks `/build` owns are implemented (tasks handed on to `/test`
  or a person are listed, not implemented);
- all selected workstreams are integrated;
- every plan checkpoint in the selected scope was executed and passed;
- executor-required verification is green;
- integrated verification is green and claimed outcomes have executed evidence;

- scoped local commits are complete, unless the user explicitly requested an
  uncommitted result (report that instruction and the remaining diff);
- the tree is in the expected state.

**BUILD BLOCKED** — in every other terminal state. Never report BUILD COMPLETE
with open blockers, skipped checkpoints, or unimplemented tasks of its own.
Both reports include:
- checkpoints executed and their outcomes;
- commits created;
- exact verification commands and outcomes;
- directly required scope expansions;
- anything noticed but intentionally untouched;
- current branch/tree state;

- the complete candidate identity required by
  `../references/target-selection.md` §Gate handoffs;

- actual run metrics when exposed: fresh executor dispatches, resumes,
  model-tier overrides, verification failures causing rework, human redirects,
  and required scope expansions.
Never estimate unavailable token/cost/time data.

Do not dispatch independent verifiers or reviewers here. The next stage is
`/test`. It verifies the candidate, or records that it is exempt.

`/build <TICKET> review fixes` fixes what the last `/review` found, instead of
planned tasks (ADR 0108). It is how a finding goes back to `/build`.
The plan checks in §1 still apply; task resume does not.

1. Run `review-sarif.py latest <TICKET> --open` (`/review` §1). It prints the
   newest round's `reviewedCommit` and its open findings. After that commit,
   HEAD may add only commits that touch `docs/reviews/` or
   `docs/tasks/<TICKET>-open.md` (`git diff --name-only <sha> HEAD`). Any
   other change means the candidate changed after the review: review it again
   first, never fix it blind. Run `review-sarif.py round <TICKET>`. When it
   prints `counted=4`, stop and report that the approach needs the user
   (ADR 0089).

2. The scope is every finding still `open` that is BLOCKER or REQUIRED and not
   pre-existing (`baselineState` is not `unchanged`), plus any ADVISORY the user
   named. Nothing else: no refactor, no plan task, no other finding.
   When the user names a pre-existing finding, recommend a follow-up ticket
   first: its fix changes behavior outside the ticket and gives the next round
   new code to review. Include it only when the user confirms after that
   warning.

3. Group findings that touch the same files into one workstream. Dispatch a
   fresh executor per workstream; never resume a build executor. Its packet
   carries, for each finding: id, `file:line`, claim, failure scenario and
   recommendation. A class finding lists every instance. It also carries the
   workstream's previous handoff report and the candidate diff (`git diff
   <candidate base>...HEAD`). When this session has no handoff report, pass
   the ticket's commit log instead.

4. The executor fixes test-first: a test that fails on the finding, then the
   fix (Prove-It). If the code is already right, it changes nothing and
   reports the finding as disputed, with `file:line` evidence; the next
   `/review` round decides. Each commit carries a `Task:` trailer naming the
   finding ids (`Task: CODE-2, SEC-1`) and the `Refs:` trailer.
   Before it reports, the executor looks for the same failure next to each
   fix: the rest of the function, its callers, and code that copies the
   pattern. It also checks that its own fix adds no new case of it. It fixes
   each new instance the same way, test-first, and lists it under the finding
   (ADR 0144).

5. Report BUILD COMPLETE with one line per finding: fixed (commit), disputed
   (evidence), or blocked (why). The plan and todo do not change. The next
   stage is `/review`.

`/build <TICKET> verify fixes` fixes the production defects the last `/test`
proved, instead of planned tasks. Use it after a **VERIFY FAIL** routed to
`/build`, with the VERIFY report pasted verbatim. The plan checks in §1 still apply; task resume
does not.

1. The scope is each `REQ-###` the VERIFY FAIL names, with its reproduction:
   expected versus actual, the failing test, or the patch artifact the
   verifier preserved. Nothing else: no plan task, no refactor, no review
   finding. A defect whose fix needs a behavior the spec does not settle is
   not fixed here: report **BUILD BLOCKED**, naming `/spec` and the REQ id.

2. Group the defects that touch the same files into one workstream. Dispatch
   a fresh executor per workstream; never resume a build executor. Its packet
   carries, per defect: the REQ id, the reproduction, expected versus actual
   and the verifier's patch when there is one; plus the candidate diff and
   the workstream's previous handoff report (the ticket's commit log when
   this session has none).

3. The executor fixes test-first: the verifier's reproduction, or a test that
   fails the same way, then the fix (Prove-It). Each commit carries a `Task:`
   trailer naming the REQ ids (`Task: REQ-017`) and the `Refs:` trailer. The
   plan and todo do not change.

4. Report **BUILD COMPLETE** with one line per defect: fixed (commit) or
   blocked (why). The next stage is `/test` again, on the new
   candidate, at the depth of the failed run or higher.

A fix or change made in conversation on a ticket branch skips this command,
so none of its records update. Record it in the same session:

- Add an `unplanned commit` item to `docs/tasks/<TICKET>-open.md` that names
  the commit's short sha (`../references/ticket-ledger.md`).

- For a behavior change, also add a `DEC-###` to the spec. Add an `Amends:`
  line when it changes an earlier rule, and set the plan to `Needs replan`.
- Run `check-ledger.py <TICKET>` before you end the session.
